<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Donbas (2014–2022)|War in Donbass]]
**[[Donetsk People's Republic]] commander [[Mikhail Tolstykh]], better known by his [[Pseudonym#Noms_de_guerre|''nom de guerre'']] "Givi", is killed in a bomb blast in [[Makiivka]], [[Donetsk Oblast]]. DPR officials blame the [[Security Service of Ukraine]] for the attack. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-38905110 (BBC)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**Six [[Afghanistan|Afghan]] [[International Committee of the Red Cross|Red Cross]] workers are shot dead by suspected [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant&nbsp;– Khorasan Province|ISIL]] militants in the northern [[Jowzjan Province]]. Two other Red Cross workers are reportedly abducted. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-38908312 (BBC)]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)]]
**Unknown gunmen storm a hotel in [[Bosaso]], leaving at least four guards and two militants dead. It is unclear who carried out the attack. An official blames [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]], though the group denies having any involvement. [http://www.aljazeera.com/news/2017/02/gunmen-kill-guards-attack-somalia-puntland-170208094641090.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**[[Syrian opposition|Syrian rebels]], with backing from the [[Turkish Armed Forces]], advance on [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]]-held [[al-Bab]], capturing the outskirts of the town. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mideast-crisis-syria-albab-idUSKBN15N0RO (Reuters)]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2015–present)|Yemeni War]]
**[[Yemen]] reassesses its permission to the [[United States]] to run [[United States special operations forces|special operations]] ground missions against suspected terrorist groups because of the civilian deaths in the January 29 raid. Earlier reports indicated permission had been suspended. [https://www.nytimes.com/2017/02/07/world/middleeast/yemen-special-operations-missions.html?_r=0 (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.nytimes.com/2017/02/08/world/middleeast/yemen-raid-american-military.html (''The New York Times''²)]

;Arts and culture
*Archaeologists from the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] announce the discovery of another [[Qumran Caves|cave]] that used to have [[Dead Sea Scrolls]]. [http://www.timesofisrael.com/new-dead-sea-scroll-cave-found-near-qumran-but-scrolls-are-gone/ (''The Times of Israel'')]

;Business and economics
*The [[United States District Court for the District of Columbia|U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia]] blocks  health insurer [[Anthem Inc.]]'s proposed $54 billion merger with rival [[Cigna]] because it would have exacerbated an already highly concentrated market and likely raised prices. [https://www.reuters.com/article/cigna-ma-anthem-idUSL1N1FU057 (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*More than 10,000 people are left homeless after a fire ravages a densely populated neighborhood of the [[Philippines]] capital [[Manila]]. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2017/02/08/shanty-town-fire-philippines-leaves-15000-homeless/ (''The Telegraph'')]

;Law and crime
*[[ 2016–17 Turkish purges]]
**The [[Cabinet of Turkey|Turkish government]] dismisses more than 4,400 public servants from their jobs in the latest purge within the country following a [[2016 Turkish coup d'état attempt|failed coup attempt last year]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/feb/08/turkey-dismisses-4400-public-servants-erdogan-trump-phone-call (''The Guardian'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2017 Romanian protests]]
**The government of [[Prime Minister of Romania]] [[Sorin Grindeanu]] survives a no-confidence motion over proposed decriminalisation of certain corruption offences, with 161 MPs voting in favor of the motion, short of the 232 votes needed for it to pass. [http://hosted.ap.org/dynamic/stories/E/EU_ROMANIA_POLITICS?SITE=AP&SECTION=HOME&TEMPLATE=DEFAULT (AP)] [http://www.aljazeera.com/news/2017/02/sdp-led-government-survives-confidence-vote-170208140726449.html (Al Jazeera)]
**Also that day, the [[Constitutional Court of Romania|Constitutional Court]] rejected two pleas made by [[President of Romania|President]] [[Klaus Iohannis|Iohannis]] and the Supreme Council of the Magistracy (CSM) that claimed an institutional conflict between the [[Parliament of Romania|Parliament]], respectively the CSM on one hand, and the [[Government of Romania|Government]] on the other, in a move that surprised the critics of the [[Social Democratic Party (Romania)|PSD]]-led cabinet and the protesters. The next day it rejected the final plea made by the [[Romanian Ombudsman|Ombudsman]] on reasons of inadmissibility. [https://web.archive.org/web/20171014133909/http://www.romaniajournal.ro/constitutional-court-rejects-ombudsmans-appeal-over-eo-13/ (''The Romania Journal'')]
*[[Somali presidential election, 2017]]
**Somali politicians gather inside a high-security compound at [[Aden Adde International Airport]] in [[Mogadishu]] to elect a [[President of Somalia|President]] for the country, with current president [[Hassan Sheikh Mohamud]] running for a second term. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2017/feb/08/somalia-goes-to-polls-president-mohamud (''The Guardian'')]
**In a surprise result, former [[Prime Minister of Somalia|Prime Minister]] [[Mohamed Abdullahi Mohamed]] is chosen as President. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-38904663 (BBC)]
*[[First cabinet of Donald Trump|Cabinet of Donald Trump]]
**The [[United States Senate]], in a 52 to 47 vote, confirms the nomination of [[Jeff Sessions]] as [[United States Attorney General]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2017/feb/08/jeff-sessions-confirmed-attorney-general-senate (''The Guardian'')]

;Science and technology

**New strong evidence supporting the existence of an [[intermediate-mass black hole]] is announced.
